questions.subject: India History
questions.question: Which Mauryan king issued the Bhabru (Bairat) edict, expressing his personal faith in the Buddha, Dhamma, and Sangha?
questions.explanation: The Bhabru edict, found near Jaipur, is one of Ashoka's minor rock edicts where he explicitly declares his reverence for the Buddha, Dhamma, and Sangha, making it a unique personal statement of his Buddhist faith.

questions.subject: India History
questions.question: The 'token currency' system, in which copper coins were issued at the value of silver coins, was introduced during the reign of which Delhi Sultan?
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Tughluq introduced the token currency system around 1329?1330 CE, issuing copper and brass coins at the face value of silver tanka; the experiment failed as people began forging coins.

questions.subject: India History
questions.question: At which session of the Indian National Congress was the famous 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) resolution passed?
questions.explanation: The Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress (December 1929), presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, passed the Purna Swaraj resolution and declared 26 January as Independence Day.

questions.subject: India History
questions.question: Which of the following Vedas is primarily a collection of melodies and chants (samans) meant to be sung during sacrificial rituals?
questions.explanation: The Samaveda is known as the 'Veda of melodies'; most of its verses are drawn from the Rigveda but are set to musical notations (samans) for singing by the Udgatri priests during soma sacrifices.

questions.subject: India History
questions.question: The 'Mansabdari system' introduced by Akbar assigned ranks to nobles. What did the term 'Sawar' rank in this system specifically indicate?
options: Number of foot soldiers to be maintained
Number of cavalry horses to be maintained
Total revenue assignment of the jagir
questions.explanation: In Akbar's Mansabdari system, each noble held two ranks: 'Zat' which determined personal status and salary, and 'Sawar' which specified the number of cavalry (horsemen) the mansabdar was required to maintain.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: At which session of the Indian National Congress was the Non-Cooperation Movement formally adopted as a resolution?
questions.explanation: The Non-Cooperation Movement was formally adopted at the Nagpur Session of the INC in December 1920, though it was first endorsed at the special Calcutta Session (September 1920). The Nagpur Session gave it full formal adoption with a revised Congress constitution.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: During the Dandi March of 1930, Mahatma Gandhi covered a distance of approximately 241 miles from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi. How many days did this march last?
questions.explanation: The Dandi March began on 12 March 1930 and ended on 5 April 1930, lasting 24 days. Gandhi walked from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi on the Gujarat coast to break the salt law.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: Which underground radio station was secretly operated during the Quit India Movement of 1942 to spread the message of freedom?
questions.explanation: During the Quit India Movement of 1942, the Congress Radio (also known as Secret Congress Radio) was clandestinely operated, notably by Usha Mehta and her associates, to spread nationalist messages when mainstream media was suppressed.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: The slogan 'Jai Hind' was popularized during the Indian freedom struggle by which leader as a battle cry of the Indian National Army?
questions.explanation: The slogan 'Jai Hind' was popularized by Subhas Chandra Bose and became the rallying cry of the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj). It was used extensively in INA broadcasts and addresses.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: The partition of Bengal announced in 1905 was carried out by which Viceroy of India, and was annulled in which year?
questions.explanation: The partition of Bengal was effected by Viceroy Lord Curzon on 16 October 1905, dividing Bengal into East Bengal and Assam, and West Bengal. It was annulled in 1911 under Lord Hardinge at the Delhi Durbar, reuniting Bengal.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following rivers does NOT originate from the Amarkantak plateau?
questions.explanation: The Tapti (Tapi) river originates from the Satpura ranges near Multai in Betul district of Madhya Pradesh, not from the Amarkantak plateau. Narmada, Son, and Johilla all originate from the Amarkantak plateau.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which type of soil is formed due to the weathering of basaltic lava rocks and is known for its high moisture-retaining capacity, making it most suitable for cotton cultivation?
questions.explanation: Black soil, also called Regur or cotton soil, is formed from the weathering of Deccan trap basaltic rocks. It has high clay content and excellent moisture-retaining capacity, making it ideal for dryland cotton cultivation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The Nathu La pass, which serves as a key trade route between India and China, is located in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Nathu La pass is located in the Sikkim Himalaya at an elevation of about 4,310 metres. It connects the Chumbi Valley of Tibet with the Gangtok region of Sikkim and was reopened for limited trade with China in 2006.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following coastal regions of India receives the majority of its rainfall during the retreating monsoon season (October-November), unlike most other parts of the country?
questions.explanation: The Coromandel Coast (southeastern coast of India, covering Tamil Nadu and parts of Andhra Pradesh) receives most of its rainfall during the retreating northeast monsoon in October-November, as it lies on the leeward side during the southwest monsoon.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Dudhwa National Park, well known as a habitat for the one-horned Indian rhinoceros and the Bengal tiger, is located in which state of India?
questions.explanation: Dudhwa National Park is situated in the Terai region of Lakhimpur Kheri district in Uttar Pradesh, along the India-Nepal border. It is a part of the Dudhwa Tiger Reserve and is notable for its reintroduced population of one-horned rhinoceros.
